chunks: Abū Baṣīr narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

He was asked about a man against whom clear evidence was established that he had committed adultery, then he fled. He said: “If he repents, then there is nothing upon him. But if he falls into the hand of the Imam before that, he carries out the hadd upon him. And if he knows his whereabouts, he sends to him.”

key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the Imam as the lawful authority who enforces judgment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a person proven guilty of adultery escapes and later repents?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a man proven by evidence to have committed adultery and then fled. It states that repentance removes liability if it occurs before capture, but if he is apprehended by the Imam beforehand, the hadd is enforced, and if his location is known, he is to be pursued.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5026 - Abu Basir narrated from Imam Abu Abdullah (as) that he was asked about a man against whom evidence was established that he had committed adultery, but then he escaped.

Imam (as) replied: "If he repents, then there is nothing upon him. However, if he is caught by the Imam before his repentance, the prescribed punishment (Hadd) will be carried out upon him. And if the Imam knows his whereabouts, he should send someone to bring him."
